intro: The vocabulary for today's couples and families, and for bringing up children.

la pareja de hecho.en: the civil partnership, the unmarried couple

bloques.texto:
**Couples.** Two people can **casarse**, with **una boda**, or be **pareja de hecho**: they **conviven** without marrying.

Before the wedding there is **una despedida de soltero** (or **de soltera**), and after it **el viaje de novios** or **la luna de miel**.

When it ends: **separarse**, **la separación**, **divorciarse**, **el divorcio**. **Tener una aventura** is to have an affair.

**How long.** **Llevan diez años juntos.** **Llevan dos años viviendo en pareja.**

**Families.** **Una madre soltera**, **un padre soltero**. **Adoptar un niño**; **un hijo adoptado**.

**Bringing up children.** **Educar** a un hijo. Small children go to **la guardería**; in the evening **un canguro** looks after them. In Spain **el canguro** and **la canguro** are the same word.

**Behaviour.** **Portarse bien** or **mal**. **Obedecer** or **desobedecer a** los padres. A child can be **travieso** (naughty, said with affection) or **maleducado** (rude, a real criticism). The opposite is **educado**.

**Careful with educado.** It means polite, not educated. A person with studies is **culto** or **con estudios**.

**Arguing.** **Discutir con** los padres. In Spanish **discutir** usually means to argue, not just to discuss.

frases.es: En casa de Rosa se juntan los domingos tres generaciones y casi todos los modelos de familia.
frases.en: At Rosa's house three generations and almost every kind of family get together on Sundays.
analisis: casi todos los modelos de familia

frases.es: Ella se casó en el jardín de su abuela hace cincuenta años y nunca pensó en separarse.
frases.en: She married in her grandmother's garden fifty years ago and never thought of separating.
analisis: se casó en el jardín de su abuela

frases.es: Su hija mayor está divorciada y es madre soltera de un niño bastante travieso.
frases.en: Her eldest daughter is divorced and is a single mother of a rather naughty boy.

frases.es: El hijo lleva doce años conviviendo con su novio: son pareja de hecho y han adoptado a una niña.
frases.en: Her son has been living with his boyfriend for twelve years: they are civil partners and have adopted a girl.

frases.es: La pequeña se casó el año pasado por lo civil y todavía habla de su luna de miel.
frases.en: The youngest married in a civil ceremony last year and still talks about her honeymoon.

frases.es: Rosa dice que lo único que pide es que los nietos se porten bien en la mesa y que nadie mire el móvil en la mesa.
frases.en: Rosa says the only thing she asks is that the grandchildren behave at the table and that nobody looks at their phone at the table.

bloques.pregunta: According to the text, who has adopted a child?
Es un chico muy educado means…

opciones.He is a very polite boy: Educado here means polite or well mannered, not educated.

bloques.correcta: He is a very polite boy

bloques.pregunta: Complete: I always obey my parents.

opciones.obedezco: Verbs in -ecer take -zc- in the first person.

bloques.pregunta: Who looks after the children when the parents go out?

opciones.el canguro: El canguro is the babysitter who looks after children while parents are out.
opciones.la guardería: That is a place for small children during the day.

opciones.texto: They have been living together for five years.
opciones.explicacion: Llevan cinco años viviendo juntos uses llevar for a period still continuing now.

opciones.texto: They take five years to live together.
opciones.explicacion: Llevar + time + gerund: to have been doing.

opciones.texto: They lived together five years ago.
opciones.explicacion: The action is still going on.

bloques.frase: Los niños se portaron muy bien en la boda
bloques.traduccion: The children behaved very well at the wedding.

bloques.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about how families have changed in your country in the last fifty years.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud on how children should be brought up: rules, freedom and obedience.
